stories.title: Equinix acquires land in Western Sydney for 150MW hyperscale campus
stories.summary: Equinix has purchased a 20-hectare site in Western Sydney for a planned 150MW data center campus, its largest land acquisition in Australia. The company cited AI-driven demand from domestic and international cloud customers.
stories.why_it_matters: Sydney's data center pipeline is the deepest in Australia, but power connection timelines are stretching toward the end of the decade. Securing land with a credible power path now is how operators stay ahead of the AI demand wave.

stories.title: Beijing tightens PUE requirements for new data centers in eastern hubs
stories.summary: Chinese regulators have issued updated guidance requiring new data centers in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen to meet a PUE of 1.25 or below, with legacy facilities given a retrofit timeline. The rules take effect in 2027.
stories.why_it_matters: Tighter efficiency rules push new Chinese capacity toward western regions and liquid cooling retrofits in the east. Operators with stranded, inefficient capacity face rising compliance costs, while cooling vendors get a multi-year demand tailwind.

stories.title: STT GDC breaks ground on 120MW campus in Bangkok
stories.summary: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres has started construction of a 120MW data center campus in Bangkok, its second facility in Thailand. The project targets enterprise and cloud demand as Thailand positions itself as a regional digital hub.
stories.why_it_matters: Thailand is emerging as the next Southeast Asian data center market after Malaysia and Indonesia, helped by government incentives and improving submarine cable connectivity. A second STT GDC campus is a strong vote of confidence in Bangkok demand.

stories.title: SK Telecom and Nvidia expand AI data center partnership in Korea
stories.summary: SK Telecom announced an expanded partnership with Nvidia to build AI data center infrastructure in Korea, including a new GPU-as-a-service offering for domestic enterprises. Financial terms were not disclosed.
stories.why_it_matters: Korean telcos are racing to become the country's AI infrastructure landlords. Partnerships with Nvidia give them preferential GPU access and enterprise distribution, raising the competitive bar for neutral colocation providers.
